pr_title: Compatibility: SQL_SELECT_LIMIT worked in show statement;
pr_body:
issue pingcap/tidb#33407
### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--
Some SHOW statements are reported with not consistant behavior with it's counterpart statement of MySQL. The issue 33407 reported 'show column from table' statement could not apply SelectLimit vars setting as MySQL does.

issue pingcap/tidb#33407
-->

Issue Number: close #33407

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?
The supported Show stmts are go through to find out what stmts should be influenced by SelectLimit value on return result set row numbers.  The Limit executor is added into plan tree for show stmts to archieve the requirement.

issue_context.title: SQL_SELECT_LIMIT worked with show columns in MYSQL but not in TIDB
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
CREATE TABLE t1(a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, d INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(1,2,3,4);
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(4,3,1,2);

SET @@sql_select_limit=1;
PREPARE stmt FROM "SHOW COLUMNS FROM t1";
EXECUTE stmt;
PREPARE stmt FROM "select * FROM t1";
EXECUTE stmt;
```
### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```sql

mysql> CREATE TABLE t1(a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, d INTEGER);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(1,2,3,4);
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(4,3,1,2);
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> 
mysql> SET @@sql_select_limit=1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> PREPARE stmt FROM "SHOW COLUMNS FROM t1";
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Statement prepared

mysql> EXECUTE stmt;
+-------+------+------+-----+---------+-------+
| Field | Type | Null | Key | Default | Extra |
+-------+------+------+-----+---------+-------+
| a     | int  | YES  |     | NULL    |       |
+-------+------+------+-----+---------+-------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> PREPARE stmt FROM "select * FROM t1";
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Statement prepared

mysql> EXECUTE stmt;
+------+------+------+------+
| a    | b    | c    | d    |
+------+------+------+------+
|    1 |    2 |    3 |    4 |
+------+------+------+------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```sql

mysql> drop table t1;

Query OK, 1 row affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> 
mysql> SET @@sql_select_limit=1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> PREPARE stmt FROM "SHOW COLUMNS FROM t1";
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> EXECUTE stmt;
+-------+---------+------+------+---------+-------+
| Field | Type    | Null | Key  | Default | Extra |
+-------+---------+------+------+---------+-------+
| a     | int(11) | YES  |      | NULL    |       |
| b     | int(11) | YES  |      | NULL    |       |
| c     | int(11) | YES  |      | NULL    |       |
| d     | int(11) | YES  |      | NULL    |       |
+-------+---------+------+------+---------+-------+
4 rows in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> PREPARE stmt FROM "select * FROM t1";
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> EXECUTE stmt;

| a    | b    | c    | d    |
+------+------+------+------+
|    1 |    2 |    3 |    4 |

1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

review_comments: Please add some comments to describe why we need to set SelectLimit to Max

Maybe using defer to recover oldSelectLimit is better.

Another question is I'm not very understand why we should set `SelectLimit` to math.MaxUint64

Yes, Have changed restore SelectLimit logic with defer.

The math.MaxUint64 is used as default of SelectLimit and it means no limit on return result set row numbers.
